newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Senate budget committee approves Eurotax.
newsitem.headline: Italian Senate budget committee approves Eurotax.

text.p: The budget committee of the Italian upper house or Senate has approved an amendment to the 1997 budget bill which inserts the so-called Eurotax into next year's deficit cutting measures, parliamentary sources said.
The sources said the Eurotax, a one-off levy on incomes designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire next year, had been approved without any substantial modifications in respect to the government's text.

The Eurotax, which is part of the 1997 budget aimed at cutting 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) from Italy's deficit next year, is aimed at whipping Italy into shape to be a founding member of a single European currency in 1999.

The entire budget, which has been through the lower house of parliament already, will be debated in the full chamber of the Senate from December 10, with voting on the measure expected on December 19.
The package will then return to the Chamber of Deputies and must be passed by both houses by law before the end of the year.
